title: Brave Search API now accepts agentic payments via the x402 protocol
content:
The Brave Search API now accepts agentic payments via the x402 protocol
The Brave Search API, our developer tool for building applications with data from the Web, is adding support for instant, pay-as-you-go, agentic payments enabled by the open x402 payment protocol. Developers and autonomous AI agents that specifically require agentic search can now programmatically query Brave’s independent search index, ground agent responses, and settle requests in real time, which eliminates the need for traditional API key management.
Integrating x402 with the Brave Search API makes it easier for an agentic harness to leverage Brave Search API via a CLI wallet, as Brave runs its own facilitator accepting USDC on the Base blockchain, with acceptance on other networks and with other stablecoins incoming soon. This allows a Brave Search API user the ability to pay for LLM Context (agentic grounding) or general web search on-demand, without first creating an account and selecting a plan. Instead, simply transfer USDC stablecoin to your agent’s wallet via the Base network and it’s ready to access the same high-quality search results powered by Brave’s search engine.
How does it work?
Brave Search API endpoints behind x402 require payment on every request rather than authentication. A request sent without payment receives an HTTP 402 Payment Required response that states the price of that search and the payment details needed to pay it. The agent signs a USDC payment for that amount and retries the request with the signed payment attached. Once the payment is verified, the search runs and results are returned with a receipt of the transaction that occurred on the Base blockchain.
Get started today
Pricing follows Brave’s published API rates: LLM Context, an API designed specifically for providing search context for agents, will cost $0.005 ($5 per 1,000). Additionally, web (search for humans), news, image, video, and local endpoints will also be available for $0.005 ($5 per 1,000). Gas fees for transacting on the Base blockchain will be covered for a limited time. Since each request carries its own payment, a Brave Search API account is no longer needed to use the service.
The easiest path to query via x402 is to install Purl Wallet, a Stripe-developed CLI wallet for your agent. Set up your wallet, top it off using Base-native USDC, and start querying today.
Ready to build pay-as-you-go search into your apps or AI agents? Check out our Brave Search x402 Proxy Documentation and explore: https://api-dashboard.search.brave.com/documentation/guides/agent-payments

report.summary: Brave now lets AI agents pay per search request through the x402 protocol, using USDC on Base and skipping API keys or accounts.
report.background: Search APIs have traditionally required developers to create accounts, manage API keys, and commit to subscription plans. That model is awkward for autonomous AI agents that may need occasional, programmatic access to fresh web data for grounding responses. The x402 protocol revives the long-dormant HTTP 402 “Payment Required” status code and pairs it with stablecoin micropayments, letting software pay for resources directly. Brave is positioning its independent search index as infrastructure for agentic AI, where an agent can discover a price, authorize a small payment, and receive results in one automated flow. The move reflects a broader push toward “agentic commerce,” where AI systems transact on behalf of users or applications without human-managed billing setup.
key_points: The payment flow is request-driven: an unpaid API call returns HTTP 402 with the search price and payment details. The agent signs a USDC payment, retries with proof attached, and receives results plus an on-chain receipt after verification on Base.

Pricing is pay-as-you-go at Brave’s published rates: $0.005 per request, or $5 per 1,000, for LLM Context and for web, news, image, video, and local search endpoints. Base gas fees are covered for a limited time.

Brave says no API account or plan is needed because each request carries its own payment. Developers and autonomous agents can query the same Brave search index for grounding or general search using a CLI wallet.

Brave runs its own x402 facilitator accepting USDC on Base, with other networks and stablecoins planned. The easiest starting path is Purl Wallet, a Stripe-developed CLI wallet, topped up with Base-native USDC.
report.impact: This signals a shift in how AI infrastructure may be sold: per-call stablecoin payments instead of seats, keys, and monthly plans. For AI developers, it lowers onboarding friction for prototypes and agentic workflows, especially when usage is sporadic or machine-initiated. But teams must now handle wallet security, crypto compliance, and payment retries alongside traditional API concerns. For the industry, it validates HTTP-native micropayments as a potential rail for agent commerce and could pressure search and data providers to support account-less, machine-payable access. For regular users, the near-term effect is indirect: AI assistants may get fresher grounding with fewer signup barriers, while crypto payment exposure and abuse controls become new trust considerations.
report.tools: Try Purl Wallet, Stripe’s CLI wallet for topping up an agent with Base-native USDC, and review Brave’s Search x402 Proxy documentation and API dashboard. Also watch the x402 protocol specs and Brave’s facilitator for support of additional networks and stablecoins.
